text_segments: Protect your home's structural integrity. Expert foundation crack repair, waterproofing, and drainage solutions.
Protect Your Home from the Ground Up

Your foundation carries the full weight of your home, and in the Pacific Northwest, it also fights a constant battle against water. The heavy rainfall, high water tables, and clay-rich soils common across Snohomish County create conditions that stress foundations year after year. Cracks develop, water finds its way in, and small problems become expensive structural issues if they are not addressed. The good news is that most foundation problems can be repaired effectively when caught early.

At NW General Contractor, we provide comprehensive foundation repair services for homeowners throughout Everett and Snohomish County. From hairline crack sealing to full structural piering, we diagnose the root cause of the problem and fix it properly. We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state, and we approach every foundation project with the thoroughness it demands — because your foundation is not something you get a second chance on.

Foundation problems come in many forms, and the right repair depends entirely on accurate diagnosis. We take the time to understand what is actually happening before recommending a solution. Here is what we handle:

— Sealing and structural repair of cracks in poured concrete walls, block foundations, and slabs. We use epoxy injection for structural cracks that need to bond back together, and polyurethane foam injection for non-structural cracks where the goal is waterproofing and flexibility.

— Exterior and interior waterproofing systems to stop water from reaching your foundation walls. Exterior waterproofing involves excavation, application of membrane or coating, and installation of drainage board. Interior systems include sealants, vapor barriers, and sump pump installation.

— Perimeter drainage systems that intercept groundwater before it reaches your foundation. We install both exterior French drains (around the foundation footing) and interior perimeter drains (inside the crawl space or basement) depending on the site conditions and the source of the water.

— Full sealing of the crawl space with heavy-duty vapor barrier, sealed vents, insulation, and dehumidification. Encapsulation prevents moisture from rising through the soil and damaging your floor joists, subfloor, and the air quality inside your home. This is one of the most impactful upgrades for Pacific Northwest homes.

— Securing your home to its foundation to prevent it from sliding off during an earthquake. Western Washington sits in an active seismic zone, and many older homes in Snohomish County are not bolted to their foundations. We install anchor bolts, Simpson hold-downs, and cripple wall bracing to meet current seismic standards.

— Repair and replacement of deteriorated piers, posts, beams, and joists in crawl space foundations. We replace rotted wood, install concrete piers, and sister or replace damaged floor joists to restore structural support under your home.

— When a foundation settles unevenly, it causes cracking, sloping floors, and structural stress throughout the home. We use steel push piers, helical piers, or slab jacking to stabilize and lift settled foundations back toward their original position.

— Repair of spalling, flaking, or deteriorated concrete on foundation walls, footings, and slabs. We remove damaged material, treat exposed rebar if present, and apply structural repair mortar or polymer-modified concrete to restore the surface.

The right repair method depends on the type of damage, the cause of the problem, and the construction of your foundation. Here is an overview of the primary methods we use and when each is appropriate.

is used for structural crack repair in poured concrete foundations. Epoxy bonds the crack back together with a material that is actually stronger than the surrounding concrete. It restores the structural integrity of the wall and creates a waterproof seal. Epoxy is rigid, which makes it ideal for cracks that are no longer moving. For cracks that are still active (seasonal expansion and contraction), we use

instead. Polyurethane remains flexible after curing, accommodating minor movement while maintaining a waterproof seal. It is the preferred method for non-structural cracks and for stopping active water leaks.

are the most effective long-term solution for persistent water intrusion. The process involves excavating down to the foundation footing, cleaning and repairing the wall surface, applying a rubberized asphalt or sheet membrane, installing a drainage board to protect the membrane and direct water downward, and backfilling with draining gravel. This method addresses water at its source — before it reaches the wall — and is the gold standard for below-grade waterproofing.

are a practical alternative when exterior excavation is not feasible or when water is entering from beneath the slab. A perimeter drain channel is installed along the interior base of the foundation wall, connected to a sump pit with an automatic pump. Water that enters is captured and pumped out before it can pool or cause damage. Interior systems are less disruptive to install and work well in combination with crawl space encapsulation.
What Does Foundation Repair Cost in Everett?

Foundation repair costs vary significantly based on the severity of the problem, the repair method required, and the accessibility of the work area. Here are the general ranges we see for projects in Snohomish County:
($500 – $2,000): Sealing hairline to moderate cracks with epoxy or polyurethane injection. Straightforward repairs that typically take a day or less.

($3,000 – $8,000): French drain installation, crawl space encapsulation, multiple crack repairs, or targeted waterproofing. These projects address ongoing moisture problems and prevent further deterioration.

($10,000 – $25,000+): Foundation piering, significant settling correction, full exterior waterproofing with excavation, or seismic retrofit. These are larger-scope projects that address serious structural concerns and protect the long-term stability of the home.

Foundation repair is not a place to cut corners. Unresolved foundation problems get worse over time, and the cost of repair increases as damage progresses. A $2,000 crack repair today can prevent a $20,000 structural repair five years from now. We provide honest assessments and will tell you if a problem is cosmetic and does not need immediate intervention.
Foundation work requires careful diagnosis before any repair begins. Treating symptoms without understanding the cause leads to recurring problems. Here is our process:

— We conduct a thorough inspection of the foundation, crawl space, and exterior grading. We check for cracks, water intrusion, settling, structural movement, moisture levels, and drainage conditions. We use levels, measuring tools, and moisture meters to build a complete picture of the situation.

— We identify the root cause of the problem — whether it is hydrostatic pressure, poor drainage, soil settlement, structural overload, or seismic vulnerability. You receive a written report with photos, measurements, and our honest assessment of the severity.

— We develop a repair plan that addresses both the symptoms and the underlying cause. The written estimate details the scope of work, materials, timeline, and cost. We explain the options and help you prioritize if budget is a concern.

— For exterior waterproofing or piering, we excavate along the foundation to the footing. We protect landscaping and hardscaping as much as possible and use proper shoring techniques to keep the excavation safe.

— Cracks are injected, membranes are applied, drains are installed, piers are driven, or structural members are replaced — whatever the plan calls for. We follow manufacturer specifications and engineering requirements for every method we use.

— After structural repairs are complete, we address water management. This may include membrane application, drain tile installation, sump pump setup, grading corrections, or crawl space vapor barrier installation.

— Excavated areas are backfilled with appropriate material (typically draining gravel near the foundation, then native soil above), compacted properly, and graded to direct surface water away from the house.

— We walk the completed work with you, explain what was done and why, provide maintenance recommendations, and hand over warranty documentation. If permits were pulled, we coordinate the final inspection with the city.
Timeline: How Long Does Foundation Repair Take?
Foundation repair timelines depend on the scope and complexity of the work. Here is what to expect for typical projects in Snohomish County:
Pier installation and settling correction: 1–2 weeks
Major structural repair with multiple components: 2–3 weeks

Weather can affect scheduling for exterior excavation work, especially during the rainy months. We plan around the forecast and protect exposed work areas when rain is expected. Interior work such as crawl space encapsulation, crack injection, and interior drainage can proceed regardless of weather conditions.
Permits for Foundation Repair in Everett
Permit requirements for foundation work depend on the nature and scope of the repair. In the City of Everett and Snohomish County, permits are generally required when the work involves:
Structural modifications to the foundation (piering, underpinning, wall reinforcement)
Seismic retrofit work (anchor bolts, hold-downs, cripple wall bracing)
Changes to the building's drainage or grading that affect neighboring properties
Alterations to the crawl space that change ventilation or fire separation

Routine maintenance such as crack sealing, waterproof coatings, and minor concrete patching generally do not require permits. We determine permit requirements during the assessment phase and handle all applications, inspections, and approvals as part of our service.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor for Foundation Repair

Foundation repair is specialized work that demands accurate diagnosis and proven methods. In Snohomish County, the combination of heavy rainfall, high water tables, and glacial till soils creates conditions that challenge foundations in ways that are specific to this region. We understand these conditions because we work in them every day. We know which soils drain and which hold water, which neighborhoods have high water tables, and which era of construction is prone to which types of foundation problems.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We do not use high-pressure sales tactics or try to scare homeowners into unnecessary repairs. We give you an honest assessment of the situation, explain your options, and help you make an informed decision. If a crack is cosmetic and does not need structural repair, we will tell you. If the problem is serious and needs immediate attention, we will explain exactly why and what the consequences of waiting would be. Our goal is to protect your home's structural integrity and give you confidence that the problem has been properly resolved.
What are the signs of foundation problems?

Common signs include cracks in interior drywall or exterior concrete, doors and windows that stick or will not close properly, uneven or sloping floors, gaps between walls and ceiling or floor, water intrusion in the basement or crawl space, and visible cracks in the foundation itself. Hairline cracks are common and often cosmetic, but horizontal cracks, stair-step cracks in block foundations, or cracks wider than a quarter inch typically indicate structural movement that needs professional evaluation.
How much does foundation repair cost in Everett, WA?

Foundation repair costs in Everett vary widely depending on the type and severity of the problem. Minor crack repair runs $500 to $2,000. Moderate repairs including waterproofing and drainage work range from $3,000 to $8,000. Major structural repairs involving piering, underpinning, or significant settling correction can cost $10,000 to $25,000 or more. We provide free inspections and detailed written estimates so you know exactly what you are dealing with before committing to any work.
Does homeowner's insurance cover foundation repair?

Standard homeowner's insurance policies typically do not cover foundation damage caused by settling, poor drainage, tree roots, or normal wear. However, foundation damage resulting from a covered event such as a burst pipe, sudden flooding, or earthquake (if you carry earthquake insurance) may be covered. We can help document the damage and provide the information your insurance company needs to evaluate a claim.

It depends on the type, size, and direction of the crack. Vertical hairline cracks in poured concrete are very common and usually result from normal curing shrinkage. They are typically cosmetic and can be sealed to prevent water intrusion. Horizontal cracks in basement walls often indicate lateral pressure from soil and water and are more serious. Stair-step cracks in block or brick foundations usually signal settling. Any crack wider than a quarter inch or one that is actively growing should be evaluated by a professional.
How can I prevent foundation problems in the Pacific Northwest?

Proper water management is the single most important factor. Make sure gutters are clean and downspouts direct water at least 6 feet away from the foundation. Grade the soil around your home so water flows away from the house. Fix any plumbing leaks promptly. Keep large trees and shrubs at a reasonable distance from the foundation. In the Pacific Northwest, installing a French drain or curtain drain system and encapsulating your crawl space are effective long-term prevention measures.
Tell us about your foundation concerns and we will get back to you within one business day.
Call us today for a free foundation inspection and honest assessment. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

text_segments: Custom detached garages, garage additions, and garage conversions. Expand your home's storage and functionality.
More Than Parking — A Garage That Works for Your Life

A garage is one of the hardest-working spaces on your property. It protects your vehicles from the Pacific Northwest weather, stores tools and equipment, serves as a workshop, and in many cases can be converted into valuable living space. If your home lacks a garage, has a garage that is too small, or has a garage that could serve a better purpose, building or converting one is a smart investment.

At NW General Contractor, we design and build custom garages throughout Everett and Snohomish County. Whether you need a new detached two-car garage, an attached garage addition, or a full garage-to-living-space conversion, we manage every phase of the project from design and permitting through construction and final inspection. We build structures that match your home, meet code, and serve your needs for decades.
Garage projects come in many forms. Some homeowners need new construction from the ground up. Others want to improve or repurpose an existing garage. Here is what we handle:
— Custom-built detached garages in single, two-car, and three-car configurations. Designed to complement your home's architecture with matching siding, roofing, and trim details.

— Adding a garage to a home that does not have one, or expanding an existing single-car garage to a two-car. Includes foundation, framing, roofing, siding, and integration with the existing structure.

— Converting an existing garage into living space such as a bedroom, home office, family room, or rental unit. Includes insulation, drywall, flooring, electrical, HVAC, and egress windows to meet residential codes.
— New garage door installation and replacement. Insulated steel, wood carriage-style, and modern aluminum doors with electric openers, keypads, and smart-home connectivity.
— Converting an unfinished garage into a comfortable, usable space with insulation, drywall, lighting, and climate control. Ideal for workshops, home gyms, and hobby spaces.
— Dedicated circuits for power tools, 240V outlets for welders and EV chargers, overhead lighting, and subpanel installation. All electrical work done to code by licensed electricians.
— New garage floor slabs, slab repair, and floor coatings. We pour reinforced concrete with proper slope for drainage and can apply epoxy or polyurea coatings for a finished, easy-to-clean surface.
— Custom workshop configurations with workbenches, tool storage, dust collection hookups, dedicated lighting, and heavy-duty electrical. We design the layout around how you work.

is the backbone of any garage. We use conventional stick-built framing with dimensional lumber, which gives us maximum flexibility in size, layout, and architectural details. Stick-built garages can be designed to match your home exactly — same roof pitch, same siding, same trim profiles. For homeowners on a tighter budget or faster timeline, pre-engineered truss packages speed up the framing phase while maintaining structural integrity.

are the largest moving component and the most visible design element. Insulated steel doors with polyurethane core are the most popular choice in Snohomish County because they provide excellent thermal performance, resist denting, and are available in dozens of styles and colors. Wood carriage-style doors offer a premium, traditional look that works especially well on craftsman and farmhouse-style homes. Modern aluminum and glass doors suit contemporary architecture and flood the interior with natural light.

matters more than most homeowners realize, even if the garage is not heated. Insulated walls and ceiling reduce temperature swings, prevent condensation on tools and stored items, and dramatically reduce road noise. If you plan to eventually convert the space above the garage to living quarters or an ADU, building with insulation from the start saves significant cost compared to retrofitting later.
What Does Garage Construction Cost in Everett?
Garage costs depend on size, site conditions, level of finish, and whether the structure includes utilities. Here are the general ranges for projects in Snohomish County:

($25,000 – $40,000): Standard 20x24 or 24x24 footprint with concrete slab, stick-built framing, composite or matching siding, asphalt shingle roof, one garage door, and basic electrical (lights and outlets).

($40,000 – $60,000): Same structure with insulated walls and ceiling, drywall, upgraded lighting, 240V circuits, epoxy floor coating, and a higher-end garage door. Suitable for workshops and hobby spaces.

($20,000 – $50,000): Converting an existing garage into a code-compliant living space including insulation, drywall, flooring, electrical upgrades, HVAC, egress windows, and potentially plumbing for a bathroom.

Adding living space above a detached garage significantly increases both cost and value. A garage with a finished apartment or ADU above can cost $80,000 to $150,000 total but adds substantial rental income potential or multigenerational living flexibility. In Snohomish County's competitive housing market, an ADU above a garage is one of the highest-ROI improvements you can make.
Building a garage is new construction, and we treat it with the same level of planning and professionalism as any addition or new build. Here is our process:

— We assess your property, discuss your needs, and create a design that meets your goals while complying with setback requirements, lot coverage limits, and building codes. We prepare construction drawings and submit permit applications on your behalf.

— The site is cleared, graded, and excavated for footings. We pour reinforced concrete footings and a slab with proper drainage slope. For sites with challenging soil or slope conditions, we engineer the foundation accordingly.
— Walls, roof trusses, and sheathing go up. The structure takes shape quickly during framing, and we schedule an inspection before closing in the walls.
— Roofing underlayment, flashing, and shingles or metal roofing are installed. We match the roofing material and color to your existing home for a cohesive look from the street.

— Siding, trim, fascia, and soffits are installed to match the house. Windows, if included, are flashed and sealed for weather protection. The garage begins to look like a permanent part of the property.
— Wiring is run for lighting, outlets, and any 240V circuits. Insulation is installed in walls and ceiling if the garage is being finished. Everything is inspected before drywall.
— If the garage is being finished, drywall goes up, the floor is sealed or coated, and any interior buildout (workbench, storage, etc.) is completed.
— The garage door is hung, the opener is mounted and programmed, and hardware is tested. We set up keypads, remotes, and smart-home integration if requested.
— We schedule the final building inspection, walk the completed project with you, and address any remaining items before we consider the project complete.
Timeline: How Long Does Garage Construction Take?
Garage construction timelines depend on the type and complexity of the project. Here is what to expect:
Detached garage (basic): 4–6 weeks from foundation to completion
Garage conversion to living space: 3–6 weeks

Permit processing in Everett and Snohomish County typically adds 2 to 4 weeks before construction can begin. Material lead times for custom garage doors, windows, and specialty items should also be factored in. We build realistic schedules and communicate any changes promptly.
Permits for Garage Construction in Everett
Garage construction always requires building permits in Everett and Snohomish County. Here is what triggers permitting requirements:
All new garage construction (attached or detached) requires a building permit
Garage conversions to living space require permits for change of use, plus electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits as applicable
Electrical work (new circuits, subpanels, 240V outlets) requires a separate electrical permit
Concrete slab work may require a grading or foundation permit depending on scope
Structures exceeding lot coverage or setback limits may require a variance from the planning department

We handle the entire permit process from initial application through final inspection. Our drawings and documentation are prepared to meet the requirements of the City of Everett and Snohomish County building departments, which helps avoid delays and revision requests.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

Garage construction is real building work — it requires foundation engineering, structural framing, weatherproofing, and code compliance. This is not a project for a handyman or an unlicensed crew. We bring the same level of professionalism to a garage build as we do to a home addition because the construction process is fundamentally the same: permitted, inspected, and built to last.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We design garages that complement your home's architecture, meet all local building codes, and serve your needs now and in the future. Whether you need basic vehicle storage or a fully finished workshop with future ADU potential, we build it right the first time.
Do I need a permit to build a garage in Everett, WA?

Yes. Any new garage construction, whether attached or detached, requires a building permit in Everett and throughout Snohomish County. Garage conversions to living space also require permits because they involve changes to the building's use and typically require electrical, plumbing, and insulation upgrades. We handle the full permit process including drawings, application, and inspections.
What is better, a detached or attached garage?

Both have advantages. Attached garages provide direct access from the house, which is convenient in the rainy PNW climate, and are generally less expensive because they share a wall with the existing structure. Detached garages offer more flexibility in size and placement, reduce noise transfer to the house, and can be designed with living space above. The best choice depends on your lot layout, budget, and how you plan to use the space.
Can I convert my garage into living space in Snohomish County?

Yes, garage conversions are allowed in most Snohomish County jurisdictions, though you will need permits and the space must meet residential building codes for insulation, egress windows, ceiling height, electrical, and ventilation. Some areas require that you maintain a minimum number of off-street parking spaces, which may limit conversion options on smaller lots. We evaluate your specific situation and advise on what is feasible.
Can I add a room or apartment above my garage?

In many cases, yes. Adding living space above a detached garage is one of the most popular ways to create an ADU (accessory dwelling unit) in Snohomish County. The garage must be engineered to support the additional load, and the living space must meet all residential codes including fire separation, egress, plumbing, and electrical. Zoning regulations vary by jurisdiction, so we verify what is allowed on your specific property.
What are the property setback requirements for a detached garage?

Setback requirements vary by jurisdiction and zoning classification. In the City of Everett, detached garages typically must be at least 5 feet from side and rear property lines, though some zones allow reduced setbacks for accessory structures. Maximum building coverage limits also apply. We verify the specific setback and coverage requirements for your property during the design phase to ensure full compliance.
Tell us about your garage project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Ready to Build Your New Garage?
Call us today for a free on-site consultation and detailed estimate. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

text_segments: Room additions, bump-outs, second-story expansions, and sunrooms. We add the space your family needs without the hassle of moving.
Expand Your Home Instead of Moving

When your family outgrows your home, the decision comes down to two options: move to a bigger house or add the space you need to the one you already have. In today's housing market, with high interest rates, limited inventory, and significant transaction costs, building a home addition is often the smarter financial choice. It is also the only option that lets you stay in the neighborhood you love while getting exactly the space you need.

NW General Contractor builds home additions throughout Everett and Snohomish County. From small bump-outs that add a few feet to a room, to full second-story additions that double your square footage, we handle every aspect of the project: design, engineering, permits, foundation, framing, and finish work.
Types of Home Additions We Build

A ground-level room addition extends your home's footprint by building a new room onto the existing structure. This is the most common type of addition and works well for adding a primary bedroom suite, a family room, a home office, or an expanded kitchen and dining area.

Room additions require a new foundation (typically a concrete stem wall or slab), which must be engineered to match or exceed the standards of your existing foundation. The new addition is framed, roofed, and finished to match the existing home in style, materials, and quality. Typical room additions range from 200 to 600 square feet.

A bump-out is a smaller addition, usually 2 to 10 feet deep, that extends an existing room. Bump-outs are ideal for expanding a kitchen, adding space to a bathroom, creating a window seat or breakfast nook, or widening a hallway. Because they are smaller in scale, they are generally faster and less expensive than full room additions.

Bump-outs under a certain size may be supported on cantilevered floor joists rather than a full foundation, which reduces cost. Larger bump-outs require foundation work similar to a full room addition. We assess the best structural approach based on the size and location of the bump-out.

A second-story addition adds an entirely new level to a single-story home. This is the most effective way to add significant square footage without expanding your home's footprint, making it ideal for properties with limited lot size or setback constraints.

Second-story additions are complex projects that require structural engineering analysis of the existing foundation and framing to ensure they can support the additional load. In some cases, foundation reinforcement or post-and-beam upgrades are needed. The existing roof is removed, new walls and floor framing are built, and a new roof is constructed.

Despite the complexity, a second-story addition is often the best value in terms of cost per square foot because it leverages your existing foundation and lot coverage. Many Everett homeowners with 1950s and 1960s ramblers use this approach to create a 3-or 4-bedroom home from a modest single-story structure.

A sunroom adds a light-filled living space that connects your home to the outdoors. In the Pacific Northwest, a properly insulated and heated four-season room can be used year-round, providing a comfortable space even during the rainy months. Sunrooms typically feature large windows or floor-to-ceiling glass on two or three sides, a solid roof, and climate-controlled comfort.

Unlike a screened porch or covered patio, a true four-season sunroom is built to the same insulation and energy code standards as the rest of your home. This means insulated walls and roof, double or triple-pane windows, and a heating system (radiant floor, mini-split, or ductwork extension).
The cost of a home addition depends on the type, size, and complexity of the project. Here are the typical ranges we see in Snohomish County:

These ranges include design, permitting, foundation, framing, roofing, exterior finish, insulation, drywall, flooring, electrical, plumbing (if applicable), and interior finish. Costs at the higher end reflect additions that include bathrooms, kitchenettes, or premium finishes.

One of the biggest concerns homeowners have about building an addition is whether it will look like it was tacked on as an afterthought. A well-designed addition should be indistinguishable from the original house. This requires careful attention to:
— The pitch, style, and material of the new roof must match or complement the existing roof. Ridge height, eave depth, and fascia details all need to align.
— We source matching siding material, or, when an exact match is unavailable, we use a complementary material that integrates naturally.
— Window style, size, and trim should be consistent with the existing home. This includes matching mullion patterns, trim profiles, and glass type.
— Flooring, trim profiles, ceiling heights, and door styles should flow seamlessly from the existing home into the addition. Abrupt transitions are the telltale sign of a poorly planned addition.
— The new foundation must bring the floor of the addition to the exact same level as the existing floor, which requires precise measurement and construction.
The foundation is the most critical element of any home addition. In Snohomish County, the most common foundation types for additions are:
Concrete stem wall with crawl space
— Matches the construction of most existing homes in the area and provides access for plumbing and HVAC.
— Used when the existing home sits on a slab or when the addition is at grade level. Requires proper compaction and drainage.
— Used in some situations where soil conditions or access constraints make traditional foundation work difficult.

Every addition foundation is engineered based on soil conditions, load requirements, and the connection to the existing structure. We work with licensed structural engineers to ensure the foundation meets all code requirements and provides long-term stability.
Permits for Home Additions in Everett

All home additions in Everett and Snohomish County require building permits. The permit process includes plan review by the building department, structural engineering review, and multiple inspections during construction (foundation, framing, insulation, electrical, plumbing, and final). We prepare all permit applications, respond to plan review comments, and schedule all inspections as part of our service.

Permit processing times in Snohomish County typically range from 4 to 8 weeks, depending on the complexity of the project and the current review backlog. We submit complete, detailed plans to minimize revision requests and keep the timeline moving.
— We visit your home, discuss your needs, review the existing structure, and talk through budget and timeline expectations.
— We develop architectural plans and coordinate structural engineering. You approve the design before we submit for permits.
— We handle all permit applications, plan review responses, and inspection scheduling.
— Excavation, forming, and pouring the foundation. This is followed by inspection and curing time.
— Walls, floor, and roof framing, followed by sheathing, roofing, and weather barrier installation.
— Electrical, plumbing, and HVAC rough-in, followed by inspections.
— Insulation, drywall, paint, flooring, trim, fixtures, and all finish work.
— We walk through the completed addition with you, address any items, and close out the project.
Add On vs. Move: Making the Right Decision

Consider the costs of selling and buying: real estate agent commissions (5-6% of sale price), closing costs on both transactions, moving expenses, and the difference in mortgage rate if your current rate is lower than today's market rate. For many Everett homeowners, the total cost of moving exceeds the cost of a well-planned addition, and the addition gives you exactly the space you need without compromising on location, school district, or neighborhood.
How much does a home addition cost in Everett, WA?

Home additions in Everett typically cost between $150 and $350 per square foot, depending on the type of addition and complexity. A 200-square-foot bump-out might cost $30,000 to $70,000, while a 500-square-foot room addition could range from $75,000 to $175,000. Second-story additions are at the higher end of the range due to structural and roofing requirements.
Do I need a permit for a home addition in Everett?

Yes, all home additions require building permits in Everett and Snohomish County. The permit process includes plan review, structural engineering approval, and multiple inspections during construction. We handle the entire permit process as part of our service.
How long does it take to build a home addition?

The construction timeline depends on the size and complexity of the addition. A bump-out takes 4 to 6 weeks. A ground-floor room addition takes 2 to 4 months. A second-story addition takes 3 to 6 months. Permit processing adds 4 to 8 weeks before construction begins.
Can you match the new addition to my existing home's architecture?

Yes, matching the existing architecture is a critical part of any addition project. We source matching or complementary roofing, siding, trim, and window styles to ensure the addition looks like it was always part of the home. We also address interior transitions so that flooring, trim profiles, and ceiling heights blend seamlessly.
Is it cheaper to add on to my house or move?

In many cases, building an addition is more cost-effective than selling and buying a different home, especially when you factor in real estate commissions, closing costs, moving expenses, and the current high-interest-rate environment. An addition also allows you to stay in a neighborhood you love and customize the space to your exact needs.
Tell us about your addition project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Need More Space? Let's Build It.
Call us today for a free in-home consultation and detailed estimate on your home addition project.

text_segments: Custom kitchen renovations designed for how you live. From layout redesign to finish details, we build kitchens that work.
Transform Your Kitchen with a Contractor You Can Trust

The kitchen is the most-used room in your home. It is where meals happen, where the family gathers, and where friends end up during every party. If your kitchen no longer works for the way you live, a well-planned remodel can change everything about your daily routine.

At NW General Contractor, we specialize in kitchen remodeling throughout Everett and Snohomish County. Whether you are updating worn-out surfaces, reconfiguring a cramped layout, or building a fully custom kitchen from the studs out, our team handles every phase of the project from design through final walkthrough.

Every kitchen remodel is different. Some homeowners want a quick facelift. Others want a complete transformation. We tailor the scope to your goals, your budget, and your timeline. Here is what we commonly handle:

— Semi-custom and fully custom cabinets in a range of wood species, finishes, and configurations. Soft-close hinges, pull-out shelving, lazy susans, and built-in organizers are all standard options we offer.
— Quartz, granite, butcher block, marble, and solid surface countertops. We template, fabricate, and install with precision seams and proper support.
— Hardwood, porcelain tile, luxury vinyl plank (LVP), and natural stone. We help you choose a material that balances durability, maintenance, and style for a high-traffic kitchen environment.
— Recessed lighting, under-cabinet LED strips, pendant fixtures over islands, and task lighting at work zones. Good kitchen lighting is functional and atmospheric.
— We coordinate with your appliance supplier to ensure proper electrical, gas, and ventilation hookups. Built-in refrigerators, range hoods, dishwashers, and microwaves are all part of the process.
— Removing walls to create open-concept living, reconfiguring the work triangle, adding islands, and improving flow between the kitchen, dining, and living areas.
— Moving sink locations, adding dedicated circuits for appliances, upgrading to GFCI outlets, and ensuring your kitchen meets current code.
— Subway tile, mosaic patterns, natural stone, and large-format porcelain. We handle the layout and installation for a clean, lasting result.
Countertop Materials: Choosing the Right Surface
The countertop is one of the most visible and most-used surfaces in your kitchen. Choosing the right material matters for both daily function and long-term satisfaction.

is the most popular choice among our Everett clients. It is engineered stone, which means it is non-porous, stain-resistant, and does not require sealing. It comes in a wide range of colors and patterns, including options that closely mimic the look of natural marble or granite. Brands like Cambria, Caesarstone, and Silestone offer extensive selections.

remains a strong option for homeowners who prefer natural stone. Each slab is unique, and granite holds up well to heat. It does require periodic sealing to maintain its stain resistance, but many homeowners appreciate the natural variation and depth of real stone.

adds warmth and character, especially in farmhouse-style or transitional kitchens. It requires more maintenance than stone surfaces, including oiling and sanding, but it can be refinished multiple times over its lifespan. Many homeowners use butcher block on an island while keeping stone on the perimeter counters.
What Does a Kitchen Remodel Cost in Everett?
Kitchen remodeling costs vary based on scope, materials, and the age of the home. Here are the general ranges we see for projects in Snohomish County:
($22,000 – $30,000): New countertops, cabinet refacing or painting, updated hardware, backsplash, and new flooring. Layout stays the same.
($30,000 – $45,000): New cabinets, stone countertops, new appliances, updated lighting, and possibly minor layout adjustments.
($45,000 – $60,000+): Structural changes, wall removal, custom cabinetry, premium materials, relocation of plumbing or electrical, and new flooring throughout.

According to the National Association of Realtors, a mid-range kitchen remodel recoups approximately 77.6% of the investment at resale. In the Snohomish County housing market, where move-in-ready homes command premium prices, a modern kitchen can significantly shorten time on market and increase buyer interest.
We follow a structured process to keep your project on track and on budget. Here is what to expect:
— We visit your home, discuss your goals, review the existing space, and talk through budget expectations. This visit is free and comes with no obligation.
— We work with you to finalize the layout, select materials, and create a detailed scope of work. You will know exactly what is included before we start.
— We handle permit applications with the City of Everett or Snohomish County, order materials, and schedule subcontractors. We confirm the start date and project timeline with you in writing.
— Existing cabinets, countertops, and flooring are removed. Framing, electrical, and plumbing rough-in work is completed and inspected.
— Cabinets are installed and leveled, countertops are templated and set, flooring goes down, and appliances are hooked up. Backsplash, lighting, and trim work follow.
— We walk the completed kitchen with you, address any punch-list items, and make sure everything meets your expectations before we call the project done.
Timeline: How Long Does a Kitchen Remodel Take?
Most kitchen remodels in Everett take between 4 and 8 weeks from the start of demolition to the final walkthrough. Here is a rough breakdown:
Countertop fabrication and installation: 1–2 weeks (template to install)
Flooring, backsplash, and finish work: 1 week
Appliance hookup and punch list: 2–3 days

Timelines can shift depending on permit processing times, material lead times (especially for custom cabinets or specialty stone), and the extent of any structural changes. We provide a detailed schedule at the start of every project and keep you updated throughout.
Permits for Kitchen Remodeling in Everett
Not every kitchen remodel requires a permit, but many do. In the City of Everett and Snohomish County, permits are generally required when the work involves:
Electrical changes (adding circuits, moving outlets, panel upgrades)
Plumbing changes (moving a sink, adding a gas line)
Structural modifications (removing or altering load-bearing walls)
Changes to ventilation or HVAC ductwork

Cosmetic updates like painting, replacing countertops on existing bases, or swapping out a faucet typically do not require a permit. We handle the permit process as part of our service, including application, inspections, and final sign-off.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

We live and work in Snohomish County. We know the local building codes, the permit process, and the challenges that come with remodeling homes built across different decades. Whether your home is a 1960s rambler or a 2010s new-build, we have the experience to handle the surprises that come with opening up walls and updating systems.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We provide detailed written estimates, maintain clean job sites, and communicate proactively throughout every project. Our goal is simple: build a kitchen you are proud of, delivered on time and on budget.
How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Everett, WA?

Kitchen remodels in Everett typically range from $22,000 for a basic refresh to $60,000 or more for a full custom renovation. The cost depends on the size of the kitchen, material selections, whether walls are being moved, and the scope of plumbing and electrical work involved.
How long does a kitchen remodel take?

Most kitchen remodels in Snohomish County take between 4 and 8 weeks from demolition to completion. A straightforward cabinet and countertop replacement may be closer to 4 weeks, while a full layout redesign with structural changes can take 8 weeks or longer.
Do I need a permit to remodel my kitchen in Everett?

Yes, permits are typically required for kitchen remodels that involve electrical work, plumbing changes, structural modifications, or moving walls. Cosmetic updates like painting or replacing countertops usually do not require permits. We handle the entire permit process for you.
What is the best countertop material for a kitchen remodel?

Quartz is the most popular countertop choice for Everett homeowners due to its durability, low maintenance, and wide range of color options. Granite remains a strong choice for natural stone appeal, while butcher block adds warmth for farmhouse or transitional styles. We help you choose the best material for your lifestyle and budget.
Will a kitchen remodel increase my home's value?

Yes. According to the National Association of Realtors, a mid-range kitchen remodel recoups approximately 77.6% of the investment at resale. In the competitive Snohomish County housing market, an updated kitchen can also help your home sell faster and attract more offers.
Tell us about your kitchen project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Call us today for a free in-home consultation and detailed estimate. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

text_segments: Outdoor Living Spaces in Everett, WA
Custom pergolas, covered patios, outdoor kitchens, and fire features. Extend your living space into the Pacific Northwest outdoors.
Bring the Indoors Out — Rain or Shine

The Pacific Northwest is one of the most beautiful places in the country, and there is no reason your outdoor space should sit unused for most of the year. With the right design — covered structures, integrated heating, proper lighting — your backyard can become a genuine extension of your home that you use nine or ten months out of the year. A well-built outdoor living space is where summer dinners happen, where you relax with coffee on a crisp fall morning, and where friends gather around a fire on a winter evening.

At NW General Contractor, we design and build custom outdoor living spaces throughout Everett and Snohomish County. From open-air pergolas and covered patios to full outdoor kitchens and fire features, we create spaces that are built specifically for the PNW climate. Every project is engineered for rain, designed for comfort, and constructed to last through decades of Pacific Northwest weather.
Outdoor living projects range from simple shade structures to full backyard transformations. We build it all, and we tailor every project to your property, your lifestyle, and your budget:

— Freestanding and attached pergolas in cedar, Douglas fir, and composite materials. Open-top designs for filtered shade, or solid-roof pergolas with polycarbonate panels for rain protection. Custom sizing, spacing, and architectural details to complement your home.

— Solid-roof covered patios that let you enjoy the outdoors regardless of weather. We build traditional gabled roofs, modern flat roofs, and shed-style designs with matching roofing and trim to integrate seamlessly with your home's architecture.

— Built-in grills, side burners, refrigerators, sinks, pizza ovens, storage cabinets, and bar seating. We build the structural framework, run gas and water lines, install electrical, and set countertops for a fully functional cooking and entertaining space.

— Custom gas and wood-burning fire pits, built-in outdoor fireplaces, and fire tables. We handle gas line installation, stone or concrete construction, and proper clearances for safe, code-compliant fire features that become the centerpiece of your outdoor space.

— Low-voltage landscape lighting, string lights on pergola structures, recessed lights in covered ceilings, step lighting, and accent lighting for pathways, plants, and architectural features. Good lighting extends usability into the evening and adds safety and ambiance.

— Concrete block, natural stone, and timber retaining walls for grade changes and terracing. Paver patios, stone walkways, and hardscape borders that define outdoor rooms and manage drainage on sloped lots.

— Enclosed outdoor rooms with screen panels that keep insects out while letting fresh air in. Ideal for dining areas, lounges, and three-season rooms. We build framed screen enclosures on existing or new patio structures.

— Reinforced concrete pads, electrical hookups, privacy screens, and access paths for hot tub installations. We ensure the pad is level, properly drained, and rated for the weight of a filled tub. Privacy enclosures in cedar or composite materials complete the setup.
Materials Built for the Pacific Northwest Outdoors

is the primary material decision for pergolas and overhead structures. Western red cedar is the traditional Pacific Northwest choice — it is naturally rot-resistant, dimensionally stable, and ages to a beautiful silver-gray patina if left untreated. Cedar accepts stain beautifully for homeowners who want to maintain the warm wood tone. Composite materials like TimberTech and Trex offer a lower-maintenance alternative that will never rot, warp, or need staining, though they cost more upfront and lack the natural warmth of real wood.
For covered structures, the roof design matters as much as the frame material. A
with asphalt shingles or standing-seam metal provides complete rain protection and can be matched to your home's existing roofing.

are a popular middle-ground option — they block rain while allowing diffused natural light to pass through, so the space does not feel dark on overcast days. For the PNW, we generally recommend solid-roof designs for primary covered patios because they offer the most weather protection and longest service life.
Outdoor kitchen materials need to withstand moisture, temperature swings, and constant use.

are the most durable options for outdoor kitchens. Stainless steel appliances and frames resist corrosion. We build outdoor kitchen islands with steel stud framing and cement board sheathing — not wood framing — to eliminate rot risk in the wet PNW climate. Stone veneer, stucco, or tile finish the exterior to match your design vision.
What Does an Outdoor Living Space Cost in Everett?
Outdoor living costs vary widely depending on the scope and complexity of the project. Here are the general ranges for projects in Snohomish County:

($5,000 – $15,000): A freestanding or attached pergola sized for a dining or lounge area. Cedar construction with optional polycarbonate roof panels. Price varies by size, material, and whether electrical (fans, lights) is included.
($10,000 – $25,000): A solid-roof structure attached to the house with proper roofing, gutters, and lighting. Size, roofing material, and ceiling finish (exposed vs. finished) affect the price.

($15,000 – $40,000+): Ranges from a basic built-in grill with counter space to a full kitchen with multiple appliances, sink, refrigerator, and bar seating. Gas line, water line, and electrical work are significant cost factors.
($2,000 – $8,000): A simple gas fire pit table starts around $2,000. Custom stone-built fire pits and full outdoor fireplaces with chimneys are at the higher end.

Outdoor living improvements typically recoup 50% to 80% of the investment at resale. In Snohomish County, where buyers actively look for homes that offer year-round outdoor usability, a covered patio with an outdoor kitchen can be a significant differentiator when your home goes on the market. These spaces signal a home that is designed for living and entertaining, not just shelter.
Outdoor living projects involve multiple trades and require careful planning to deliver a space that functions as well as it looks. Here is our process:

— We visit your property, discuss how you want to use the space, assess the existing conditions (slope, drainage, sun exposure, proximity to the house), and develop a design concept. We discuss materials, features, and budget to align expectations before any work begins.

— We evaluate soil conditions, drainage patterns, utility locations, and structural tie-in points if the project attaches to the house. For sloped lots, we plan grading and retaining solutions. For covered structures, we assess the best attachment method to the existing roof or framing.

— We prepare construction drawings and submit permit applications to the City of Everett or Snohomish County. Projects with covered roofs, electrical, gas, or plumbing each require separate permits. We manage the entire permit process and schedule inspections throughout construction.

— Concrete footings are poured for posts, columns, and any freestanding structures. Patio slabs and paver bases are prepared with proper compaction and drainage. Foundation work is inspected before framing begins.

— Posts, beams, rafters, and roofing go up. For covered patios, the roof is tied into the house properly with flashing to prevent leaks. Pergola framing is assembled, leveled, and secured. This is when the project starts to take its final shape.

— Gas lines for grills, fire pits, and heaters are run by licensed plumbers. Electrical circuits for lighting, outlets, fans, and appliances are wired by licensed electricians. Water lines for sinks and prep stations are plumbed. All utilities are inspected before being covered.

— Countertops are installed, appliances are set and connected, lighting fixtures are mounted, and all finish materials (stone veneer, stucco, tile, stain) are applied. Fire features are tested and adjusted.
— The new outdoor space is connected to the surrounding landscape with pathways, plantings, gravel borders, or sod. Drainage is verified to ensure water flows away from the structure and the house.

— We walk the completed project with you, demonstrate all systems (gas, electrical, lighting controls), and verify everything meets your expectations. Punch-list items are addressed before we close out the project.
Timeline: How Long Does an Outdoor Living Project Take?
Timelines depend on the complexity of the project and the number of trades involved. Here is what to expect:
Outdoor kitchen: 4–8 weeks (including utility rough-in and countertop fabrication)
Full backyard transformation (covered patio + kitchen + fire feature + lighting): 6–10 weeks

Permit processing in Everett and Snohomish County adds 2 to 4 weeks before construction can begin. Weather is also a factor — we schedule concrete and roofing work during dry stretches and protect unfinished work during rain. Material lead times for specialty items like custom stone, premium appliances, and fabricated countertops should be factored into the overall timeline. We build a detailed schedule at the start and keep you informed throughout.
Permits for Outdoor Living Projects in Everett
Many outdoor living features require permits in Everett and Snohomish County. Here is what typically triggers a permit requirement:
Any structure with a roof (covered patios, solid-roof pergolas) requires a building permit
Gas line installation for grills, fire pits, and heaters requires a plumbing/mechanical permit
Electrical work for lighting, outlets, and appliances requires an electrical permit
Water and drain lines for outdoor sinks require a plumbing permit
Retaining walls over 4 feet in height require a building permit with engineered drawings
Structures within setback zones may require a variance or special approval

Simple features like a portable fire pit, string lights on an existing structure, or a freestanding open-top pergola under a certain size may not require permits, but it varies by jurisdiction. We verify the specific requirements for your project and handle all permit applications and inspections as part of our service.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

Outdoor living projects involve structural work, roofing, electrical, gas, plumbing, concrete, and finish carpentry — often all on the same project. This is not a job for a landscaper or a handyman. It requires a licensed general contractor who can coordinate multiple trades, pull permits, manage inspections, and deliver a space that is safe, code-compliant, and built to last through years of Pacific Northwest weather.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We have built outdoor living spaces on flat lots, steep hillsides, and everything in between throughout Snohomish County. We design for the PNW climate specifically — rain protection, proper drainage, moisture-resistant materials, and heating options that let you use the space year-round. If you want an outdoor space that is more than just a patio with a chair on it, we are ready to build it.
Can I use my outdoor living space year-round in the Pacific Northwest?

Yes, with the right design. A covered patio or pergola with a solid roof keeps rain off, and adding heaters, a fire feature, or a screened enclosure extends usability into the cooler months. Many of our clients in Snohomish County use their outdoor spaces 9 to 10 months a year with proper coverage and heating. The key is building for the PNW climate from the start, not trying to retrofit protection later.
What are the best covered patio options for the rainy Pacific Northwest?

For the PNW, a solid-roof covered patio is the best investment. Options include a traditional framed roof with asphalt shingles to match the house, a modern flat roof with a membrane system, or insulated aluminum patio covers for a lower-cost solution. Polycarbonate panels are a good middle ground, providing rain protection while letting filtered natural light through. We recommend a minimum roof pitch of 2:12 for proper drainage.
How much does an outdoor kitchen cost to build?

Outdoor kitchens in Snohomish County typically range from $15,000 for a basic setup with a built-in grill, counter space, and storage to $40,000 or more for a full kitchen with a grill, side burner, refrigerator, sink, pizza oven, and premium countertops. The cost depends on the size of the kitchen, the appliances selected, countertop material, whether gas and water lines need to be run, and the complexity of the structure housing the kitchen.
Do I need a permit for a pergola or covered patio in Everett?

In most cases, yes. Structures with a roof, including covered patios and solid-roof pergolas, typically require a building permit in Everett and Snohomish County. Open-top pergolas without a solid roof may be exempt depending on size and location, but it varies by jurisdiction. Any project involving electrical, gas, or plumbing also requires separate trade permits. We verify requirements and handle all permit applications as part of our service.
What is the ROI on an outdoor living space?

Outdoor living improvements typically recoup 50% to 80% of the investment at resale, depending on the scope and quality of the project. In the Snohomish County housing market, well-designed outdoor spaces are a strong selling feature because they extend the usable living area of the home. Covered patios and outdoor kitchens are particularly attractive to buyers because they signal a home that is ready for entertaining year-round.
Tell us about your outdoor living project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Ready to Create Your Dream Outdoor Space?
Call us today for a free on-site design consultation and detailed estimate. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

text_segments: Interior & Exterior Painting in Everett, WA
Professional painting services that transform your home inside and out. Expert prep, premium paints, lasting results.
Fresh Paint Changes Everything About a Home

Nothing transforms a space faster or more dramatically than a professional paint job. A fresh coat of paint can make a tired room feel brand new, boost your curb appeal from the street, and protect your home from the elements. In the Pacific Northwest, where rain and moisture are a constant, quality painting is not just cosmetic — it is essential maintenance that protects your investment.

At NW General Contractor, we provide comprehensive interior and exterior painting services throughout Everett and Snohomish County. We use premium paints, invest serious time in surface preparation, and deliver clean, lasting results that hold up to the PNW climate. Whether you need a single accent wall or a complete exterior repaint, we handle every step from color consultation to final cleanup.

Every painting project has different needs. Some homeowners want a quick refresh. Others are preparing to sell or just moved into a home that needs a total color overhaul. We scale our services to match your goals and budget:
— Walls, ceilings, trim, doors, and closets. We protect your floors and furniture, cut clean lines, and apply two coats of premium paint for even, lasting coverage in every room.
— Full exterior repaints including siding, trim, fascia, soffits, and gutters. We power-wash, scrape, prime, and caulk before applying weather-resistant paint rated for the Pacific Northwest climate.
— A cost-effective alternative to replacing kitchen or bathroom cabinets. We sand, prime, and spray multiple coats of durable enamel for a factory-smooth finish that holds up to daily use.
— Cedar and composite deck staining, sealing, and restoration. We clean the surface, apply UV-resistant stain, and seal against moisture to extend the life of your deck in our wet climate.
— Driveways, walkways, siding, fences, and patios. Pressure washing removes years of moss, mildew, and grime and is often the first step before any exterior painting project.
— Patching holes, fixing cracks, skim-coating damaged areas, and matching existing wall textures. We make the repairs invisible before the paint goes on.
— Crown molding, baseboards, window casings, door frames, and decorative accents. Detail work that requires a steady hand and careful masking for crisp, professional edges.

— Not sure what colors to choose? We help you select palettes that complement your home's architecture, lighting, and style. We can provide sample swatches applied directly to your walls so you can see the color in your space before committing.
Premium Paints Built for the Pacific Northwest

The paint you choose matters as much as the skill of the painter. In the Pacific Northwest, moisture, rain, and limited sun exposure put unique demands on both interior and exterior coatings. We use professional-grade paints from Benjamin Moore and Sherwin-Williams because they perform consistently in our climate and offer the best color retention and durability.

For exteriors, we recommend 100% acrylic latex formulas with built-in mildew resistance. Products like Benjamin Moore Aura Exterior and Sherwin-Williams Duration provide excellent adhesion, resist cracking and peeling, and maintain their color despite months of overcast skies and rain. For homes in heavily shaded areas where moss and algae growth are common, we use coatings with antimicrobial additives to slow biological growth on painted surfaces.

Choosing the right sheen is also important. Flat finishes hide surface imperfections and work well on ceilings and low-traffic walls. Eggshell and satin are ideal for living rooms, bedrooms, and hallways because they are easier to clean while still providing a subtle finish. Semi-gloss is the standard for kitchens, bathrooms, trim, and doors because it resists moisture and wipes clean easily. We walk you through these choices so you get the right product in every room.
What Does a Painting Project Cost in Everett?
Painting costs depend on the size of the area, the condition of the surfaces, and the quality of materials selected. Here are the general ranges we see for projects in Snohomish County:
($400 – $800): One standard bedroom or living room including walls, ceiling, and trim. Two coats of premium paint, all prep work included.
($3,000 – $8,000): Full interior repaint for a typical 3–4 bedroom home. Price varies based on room count, ceiling height, trim detail, and the amount of prep required.
($5,000 – $12,000): Complete exterior repaint including siding, trim, fascia, and soffits. Includes power washing, scraping, priming, caulking, and two coats of exterior paint.

A well-executed exterior paint job is one of the highest-ROI home improvements you can make. The National Association of Realtors consistently ranks exterior painting among the top projects for cost recovery at resale. In Snohomish County, where curb appeal directly impacts buyer perception, a fresh exterior can add thousands of dollars in perceived value and help your home sell faster.
A paint job is only as good as the preparation behind it. We follow a detailed process that ensures clean results and long-lasting performance:
— We visit your home, discuss your vision, review the surfaces, and help you select colors and sheens. You receive a detailed written estimate with no surprises.

— This is where the real work happens. We sand rough areas, scrape peeling paint, fill holes and cracks, caulk gaps around trim and windows, and apply primer where needed. For exteriors, we power-wash the entire surface first.
— We mask off trim, cover floors with drop cloths, protect fixtures and hardware, and tape clean lines at transitions. Your furniture, carpets, and landscaping are fully protected.

— Two full coats of premium paint applied with brushes, rollers, or sprayers depending on the surface. We back-brush all sprayed areas for proper adhesion and use the right application method for each surface type.
— We cut in around fixtures, outlets, and trim with precision. All edges are clean and straight. Any spots that need attention get touched up before we consider the room complete.

— We walk the entire project with you, check every surface under good lighting, and address any punch-list items. All tape, drop cloths, and materials are removed. We leave your home cleaner than we found it.
Timeline: How Long Does a Painting Project Take?
Painting timelines depend on the scope of the project and the amount of prep work required. Here is what to expect for typical projects:
Cabinet painting: 1–2 weeks (includes cure time between coats)

Exterior painting in the Pacific Northwest is weather dependent. We schedule exterior work during dry stretches and monitor forecasts closely. Paint needs to be applied when temperatures are above 50°F and rain is not expected within 4 to 6 hours. We plan around the weather so you get a finish that adheres properly and lasts as long as it should.
Painting alone does not typically require a building permit in the City of Everett or Snohomish County. However, there are a few situations where permits or approvals may come into play:
Homes in historic districts may require approval for exterior color changes
HOA-governed communities may have color restrictions and review processes
Commercial properties may require permits for scaffolding or lane closures
Lead paint abatement (in homes built before 1978) must follow EPA RRP rules and may require certification

For residential painting projects, you can typically move forward without any permits. If your project involves drywall repair, electrical updates, or structural work in addition to painting, those components may require separate permits. We advise you on what is needed during your estimate.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

We are not a crew that shows up, slaps on a coat of paint, and leaves. We are a full-service general contractor with painters who understand that preparation is the foundation of a lasting finish. Our crews are experienced with every type of surface common in Snohomish County homes — from old-growth cedar siding on mid-century ramblers to modern fiber cement on new construction.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We use premium materials, maintain clean job sites, and stand behind our work. If you want a painting contractor who takes the time to do it right, gives you a detailed estimate upfront, and delivers results that hold up year after year in the PNW climate, we are the team to call.
How often should I repaint my home's exterior in the Pacific Northwest?

In the Pacific Northwest, exterior paint typically lasts 5 to 7 years due to the high moisture, rain, and limited direct sun. Homes with south-facing or west-facing walls may need attention sooner. Using premium moisture-resistant paint and proper surface preparation can extend that timeline closer to 8 to 10 years.
What is the best paint for humid climates like Everett?

For humid climates like Snohomish County, we recommend 100% acrylic latex paints with mildew-resistant additives. Benjamin Moore Aura and Sherwin-Williams Duration are both excellent choices that resist moisture penetration and maintain color integrity despite the rain and humidity common in the PNW.
How long does interior paint last before it needs to be redone?

Interior paint in well-maintained homes typically lasts 7 to 10 years. High-traffic areas like hallways, kitchens, and kids' rooms may show wear sooner and benefit from higher-sheen, washable finishes. Bathrooms and laundry rooms should use moisture-resistant formulas to prevent peeling.
Why is surface preparation so important before painting?

Surface preparation is the single most important factor in a lasting paint job. Skipping prep leads to peeling, bubbling, and poor adhesion within a year or two. Proper prep includes washing, scraping loose paint, sanding rough areas, filling cracks and nail holes, caulking gaps, and applying primer. We spend significant time on prep because it determines how long the paint lasts.
What factors affect the cost of a painting project?

The main cost factors are the total square footage being painted, the condition of the surfaces (how much prep is needed), the number of colors and accent details, the type and quality of paint selected, ceiling height and accessibility, and whether any drywall repair or texturing is required before painting.
Tell us about your painting project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Ready to Transform Your Home with Fresh Paint?
Call us today for a free estimate on your painting project. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.
